title_th: ซักรีดและซักแห้ง
recycles: days of the week and clock times
clarification questions: 'Sorry, could you say that again?'
register: casual-polite service-counter English (first-name-free, friendly, transactional; short turns)

targets.why_it_matters_here: The whole transaction is carried by the endings. 'Two shirts pressed' with dropped finals becomes 'two shirt press' — the counter staff writes down one item, wash only, and you come back to one un-ironed shirt and pay a second time. 'Washed' vs 'wash' is also the difference between 'it's already done' and 'please do it'.

You say your ticket number out loud and you hear the price and the pick-up day exactly once. Say 'thirty' when your ticket is 'thirteen' and you are handed a stranger's clothes; hear 'fifteen' when the price is 'fifty' and you arrive at the counter without enough money.

model_dialogues.label: Dropping clothes off — standard counter visit

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Hi there, what can I do for you?
lines.th: สวัสดีค่ะ มีอะไรให้ช่วยคะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: I'd like these washed, please.
lines.th: ขอซักพวกนี้หน่อยครับ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Sure. Two shirts and a jacket, yeah?
lines.th: ได้เลย เสื้อเชิ้ตสองตัวกับแจ็คเก็ตหนึ่งตัวใช่มั้ย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Yes. And this shirt has a stain.
lines.th: ใช่ครับ แล้วเสื้อตัวนี้มีรอยเปื้อนด้วย

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: On the collar — I see it. We'll have a go. That's fifteen dollars.
lines.th: ตรงคอเสื้อ เห็นแล้ว เดี๋ยวลองดูให้ ทั้งหมดสิบห้าเหรียญ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, fifteen or fifty?
lines.th: ขอโทษนะ สิบห้าหรือห้าสิบ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Fifteen. Five-oh would be a bit rough!
lines.th: สิบห้า ถ้าห้าสิบนี่โหดไปหน่อยแล้ว!

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay. When will it be ready?
lines.th: โอเค แล้วจะเสร็จเมื่อไหร่

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Thursday after five. Here's your ticket — don't lose it.
lines.th: วันพฤหัสหลังห้าโมง นี่ใบรับของ อย่าทำหายนะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thursday after five. Thanks.
lines.th: วันพฤหัสหลังห้าโมง ขอบคุณครับ

model_dialogues.label: Picking up — the stain is still there and the price has changed

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Afternoon. Have you got your ticket?
lines.th: สวัสดีตอนบ่าย เอาใบรับของมามั้ย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Here it is. Number thirty-one.
lines.th: นี่ครับ เบอร์สามสิบเอ็ด

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Thirty-one… hang on. Right — two shirts and the jacket.
lines.th: สามสิบเอ็ด… เดี๋ยวนะ อ้อ ได้แล้ว เสื้อเชิ้ตสองตัวกับแจ็คเก็ต

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thanks. Can I check them?
lines.th: ขอบคุณครับ ขอเช็คหน่อยได้มั้ย

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Go ahead, take your time.
lines.th: เชิญเลย ดูตามสบาย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry — the stain is still here.
lines.th: ขอโทษนะ รอยเปื้อนยังอยู่เลย

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Ah, on the collar. That was coffee, wasn't it? Some stains don't come out first go.
lines.th: อ๋อ ตรงคอเสื้อ อันนี้กาแฟใช่มั้ย รอยบางอย่างมันไม่ออกตั้งแต่รอบแรกหรอก

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Can you try again?
lines.th: ลองซักอีกรอบได้มั้ย

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: We can, but you'd get it Monday. Is that alright?
lines.th: ได้ แต่ต้องมารับวันจันทร์นะ โอเคมั้ย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Monday's fine. Is there a charge?
lines.th: วันจันทร์ก็ได้ครับ ต้องจ่ายเพิ่มมั้ย

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: No charge for a re-clean. But there's a bit extra on the jacket — it's silk, so it's hand-finished. Fourteen instead of ten.
lines.th: ซักซ้ำไม่คิดเงิน แต่แจ็คเก็ตแพงขึ้นนิดนึง เป็นผ้าไหม ต้องรีดมือ เป็นสิบสี่ ไม่ใช่สิบ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, fourteen or forty?
lines.th: ขอโทษนะ สิบสี่หรือสี่สิบ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Four-teen. One four.
lines.th: สิบ-สี่ หนึ่งกับสี่

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay. So what's the total today?
lines.th: โอเค วันนี้รวมทั้งหมดเท่าไหร่

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Thirty-four dollars all up, and nothing to pay on Monday.
lines.th: สามสิบสี่เหรียญครบ วันจันทร์ไม่ต้องจ่ายอะไรอีก

lines.text: Can I pay by card?
lines.th: จ่ายบัตรได้มั้ย

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Course you can. Tap there. And keep this ticket for Monday.

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Got it. Monday after five?
lines.th: โอเคครับ วันจันทร์หลังห้าโมงใช่มั้ย

lines.text: We shut at six, so any time before that.
lines.th: ร้านปิดหกโมง มาก่อนหกโมงก็ได้

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Great. Thanks very much.
lines.th: เยี่ยมเลย ขอบคุณมากครับ

chunk_drills.label: Asking for a service (causative get)
examples: Can I get these washed?
Can I get this dry cleaned?
Can I get these shirts pressed?
Can I get this jacket cleaned by Friday?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: get + past participle; the -ed/-t ending must be audible or the service changes

chunk_drills.label: Reporting a problem
chunk_drills.pattern: There's a stain on the + [part of the item].
examples: There's a stain on the collar.
There's a stain on the sleeve.
There's a mark on the cuff.
A button is missing on this shirt.
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: there is + prepositional phrase; recycles clothing/body-part location language

chunk_drills.label: Time and readiness
chunk_drills.pattern: When will it be ready? / Will it be ready by + [day/time]?
examples: When will it be ready?
Will it be ready by Friday?
Can I pick it up tomorrow morning?
Do you do same-day?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: will for scheduled future; recycles days of the week and clock times

chunk_drills.label: Price checking
chunk_drills.pattern: How much is it per + [item]? / What's the total?
examples: How much is it per shirt?
How much is it per kilo?
Is express extra?
What's the total?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: recycles 'How much…?' and prices; forces teen/ty discrimination in the answer

chunk_drills.label: Clarifying a number (the safety chunk)
examples: Sorry, did you say fifteen or fifty?
Sorry, thirteen or thirty?
Could you say that again, please?
Could you write it down?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: recycled clarification routine from earlier units; alternative question intonation

guided_roleplay.learner_role: Customer dropping off two shirts and a silk jacket, then coming back to collect them
flow: Step 1 — Greet and state what you want: 'Hi, can I get these washed, please?'
Step 2 — Confirm the items and count them out loud (two shirts, one jacket).
Step 3 — Point out the stain and say where it is (collar / sleeve).
Step 4 — Ask the price: 'How much is it per shirt?' and repeat the number back.
Step 5 — Ask when it will be ready and repeat the day and time back.
Step 6 — Take the ticket; at pick-up, say your ticket number and check the clothes before you leave.
Step 7 — If something is wrong, ask for a re-clean and ask if there is a charge.
sentence_frames: Hi, can I get these ___, please?
Sorry — the stain is still here. Can you try again?
Is there a charge for that?

free_roleplay.ai_persona: Counter staff at a busy neighbourhood dry cleaner. Friendly, quick, a bit rushed; uses short service-counter turns, says prices and days once, and expects the customer to check their own items.
free_roleplay.a2_behavior: Keeps to the standard script: takes the items, counts them back, quotes a simple price, gives one pick-up day and time, hands over a ticket. Repeats numbers clearly if the learner asks.
b1_curveballs: The stain can't be fully removed — offers a re-clean for Monday instead.
The silk jacket costs more than the price on the sign because it is hand-finished.
Asks a choice question the learner didn't expect: 'On hangers or folded?'
Asks for a phone number and reads it back with one digit wrong.
The card machine is down — cash only today.
The learner has lost the ticket; staff asks for a name and a description of the items.
One item is not ready and has to be collected the next day.

roleplay_rubric.criterion: Completed the full transaction: stated the service, confirmed the items and count, got a price, and got a pick-up day/time
Reported the problem clearly — named the stain and its location on the garment
Repeated back or confirmed at least one number (price, ticket number, or time) so it could be checked
Asked at least one clarification question ('Sorry, fifteen or fifty?' / 'Could you say that again?') instead of nodding through
Register stayed casual-polite: 'Can I get…', 'please', 'thanks' — no commands to the staff
Pronunciation: final consonants and clusters audible ('shirts', 'washed', 'pressed', 'silk', 'ticket') and teen/ty numbers distinguishable
Coped with a curveball (re-clean, extra charge, cash only, lost ticket) — negotiated a new day or price without abandoning the conversation

register_culture_note.en: A laundry counter is fast and informal. Short turns win: 'Hi, can I get these washed?' is complete and polite. You are expected to say the number of items out loud, to repeat prices and days back, and — at pick-up — to open the bag and look before you leave the shop. Checking your own clothes at the counter is normal customer behaviour, not distrust.

do_dont.prefer: Can I get this washed by tomorrow, please?

do_dont.avoid: Two shir', please. (finals dropped — staff logs one item, wash only)
do_dont.prefer: Two shirts, washed and pressed, please.

do_dont.avoid: Nodding and saying 'yes' when you didn't catch the price
do_dont.prefer: Sorry, did you say fifteen or fifty?

do_dont.avoid: This is very dirty, you must clean it.
do_dont.prefer: There's a stain on the collar — can you get it out?

do_dont.avoid: Saying nothing about a bad result and leaving quietly
do_dont.prefer: Sorry — the stain is still here. Can you try again?

register_culture_note.thai_cultural_note: In Thailand many laundry shops price by the kilo, know their regulars, and will sort things out informally later. Abroad, dry cleaners usually price per item and run on the paper ticket: no ticket, slow problem. Two habits follow from that difference — say your item count and your ticket number clearly, and raise a problem at the counter on the day rather than waiting to avoid making a fuss. Complaining politely on the spot is the expected, easiest route to a free re-clean; a week later it is much harder.

can_do_checkpoints.statement: I can drop off clothes and say what service I want (wash / dry clean / press).
I can ask how much it costs per item and understand the total.
I can ask when it will be ready and repeat the day and time back correctly.
I can point out a stain or damage, say exactly where it is, and ask for a re-clean.
I can handle a change of plan — a higher price, a later day, or cash only — and agree on new arrangements.
My final consonants ('shirts', 'washed', 'pressed', 'ticket') and my teen/ty numbers are clear enough that the counter writes down the right order.
